one_liner: GNU's embeddable Scheme with a JIT; about 2x faster than PUC Lua 5.4.7 on a naive fib(47) shootout.
what_it_does: Guile is the GNU project's extension language: a Scheme implementation shipped as a C library (libguile) plus the guile command, meant to be linked into C programs as their scripting layer. A host enters Guile with scm_with_guile or scm_init_guile, exposes C functions with scm_c_define_gsubr, and loads or evaluates Scheme code. It is a different language and C API from Lua, so it replaces Lua only by rewriting scripts and bindings.
how_it_is_fast: Source is compiled ahead of running to Guile 3's low-level bytecode (auto-compiled into $XDG_CACHE_HOME/guile/ccache on first load), and hot code is then translated to native code by a JIT built on the lightening library, enabled by default on x86-64, i686, ARMv7 and AArch64; NEWS credits the JIT with up to 4x over Guile 2.2. The lower-level instruction set lets the compiler elide type checks and unbox integers, and 3.0.8 added cross-module inlining. PUC Lua, the baseline, is a pure bytecode interpreter, so the fib gap is largely JIT versus interpreter.
when_to_use: C or C++ applications on Linux or the BSDs that want a full Scheme (modules, hygienic macros, continuations, threads, FFI via (system foreign)) as their extension language, and can live with LGPL linking.
Call-heavy, integer-heavy script code where a JIT pays off: drujensen/fib puts guile at 102.9 s vs lua at 203.7 s for naive fib(47).

Projects choosing among Scheme engines: on ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks all.csv, Guile 3.0.11 is about 14x faster than Chibi-Scheme 0.11.0 (geomean over 44 shared benchmarks) and about 2.3x faster than s7 11.3 (51 shared), derived from page data.
GNU-ecosystem tools (Guix-style workflows, GNU programs with Guile hooks) where Guile is already installed as a distro package (guile-3.0).
when_not_to_use: You need the fastest small dynamic language: LuaJIT 2.1.1 runs the same fib(47) in 37.8 s, 2.7x faster than Guile; Chez Scheme is about 2.6x faster than Guile 3.0.11 across r7rs-benchmarks (derived from page data).
Tiny footprint or easy vendoring: libguile needs libgmp, libiconv, libintl, libltdl, libunistring, libgc (Boehm-Demers-Weiser, at least 7.2) and libffi, against Lua's single directory of ANSI C.
Closed-source static linking: LGPL-3.0-or-later obliges you to allow relinking.
Your scripts and bindings are already Lua: there is no compatibility layer, so the swap is a rewrite.
Short-lived processes where start-up and first-run auto-compilation matter; the shootout times whole processes but says nothing about start-up cost separately.

integration.dependencies: libgmp, libiconv, libintl, libltdl, libunistring, libgc (bdw-gc 7.2+), libffi, pkg-config at build time; libreadline optional
integration.min_toolchain: GNU autotools build (./configure); minimum compiler version not documented in the README read; prebuilt as the guile-3.0 package on Debian/Ubuntu
integration.platforms: JIT on x86-64, i686, ARMv7 and AArch64 (NEWS for 3.0.0), RISC-V added in 3.0.11 (search snippet); builds on GNU/Linux, FreeBSD (README notes), macOS and 64-bit Cygwin per NEWS; interpreter-only elsewhere
integration.thread_safety: Threaded by default on a threaded libgc build (README shows --without-threads for single-threaded builds); host threads enter Scheme through scm_with_guile and leave with scm_without_guile

gotchas: Harness flaw: drujensen/fib's run.sh runs every :interpreted entry, Guile and Lua included, only once ('Running #{lang.name} 1 time', unchanged since the 2021-04-17 commit 'add compile times. average 5 runs'), although the README says all languages run 5 times; the 102.887 s and 203.702 s figures are single runs, not averages. With runs of 100 to 200 s the noise is small against a 2x gap, but nothing was repeated.

The shootout files Guile under 'Interpreted, dynamically typed', but Guile 3 JIT-compiles by default on x86-64, so this is a JIT against the PUC interpreter, not interpreter against interpreter; the single timed run also includes the first-load auto-compilation of fib.scm (small for a five-line file).
libgc is a conservative collector: C stacks and heap words that look like pointers keep objects alive, which eases embedding but can retain memory.

The catalogued URL is a stale unofficial GitHub mirror (NEWS stops at 3.0.9, last commit 2022-04-08); the benchmark used Ubuntu's Guile 3.0.10 and 3.0.11 shipped on 2025-12-01 (search snippet; gnu.org, lists.gnu.org and codeberg.org are blocked here), so take sources from the official release tarballs, not this mirror.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Guile over Chibi-Scheme or s7 when you want a Scheme and speed matters more than size: on r7rs-benchmarks it is about 14x faster than Chibi and 2.3x faster than s7 (derived from page data), while Chibi and s7 are far smaller to embed. Pick LuaJIT or Luau instead when the language is open and you want the fastest small embeddable runtime.
verified_claims_summary: One naive recursive fib(47) run per interpreter in drujensen/fib (whole-process bash time, 2024-12-05, ubuntu:24.04 container on a Hetzner CCX23 with 4 vCPU 'Intel Xeon 3.1Ghz'): Guile 3.0.10 from the Ubuntu package 102.887 s versus Lua 5.4.7 built by asdf 203.702 s, about 2.0x (derived from page data); LuaJIT 2.1.1 37.837 s.
status_note: Guile itself is maintained (3.0.11 released 2025-12-01 per search snippet) and LGPL-3.0-or-later, but the catalogued GitHub mirror stopped in 2022, so build from GNU release tarballs or distro packages.
